newsitem.title: USA: Cable & Wireless Comms in N.Y. debut.
newsitem.headline: Cable & Wireless Comms in N.Y. debut.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Communications, Britain's new cable telephone and television group, made a low-key debut Monday on the New York Stock Exchange.
The company's American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) were unchanged at 24-5/8 in late afternoon. Volume was only 300 ADRs.
Traders said most investors were unaware that the stock -- part of a free float of 14.7 percent of the new group -- had started on the exchange.
"There is just no liquidity," a trader said.
The company was formed last year by merging the Mercury unit of Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc with the three British cable television units of NYNEX Corp and Bell Canada, a unit of BCE Inc.
Cable and Wireless said Friday that more than 95 percent of North American investors had accepted share offers in the new company.
The new company's shares closed at 299.5 pence in London, barely changed from their opening at 300 pence.
